new_task_1.title: Handle unknown remote HTTP error codes with a ConanException
new_task_1.description: Conan 2.27.0 fixes remote error handling so unexpected HTTP status codes returned by a server are surfaced as a regular ConanException that includes the status code and server response text, instead of failing through the unmapped exception path.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that operations talking to Conan remotes fail cleanly when the server returns an HTTP status code that is not mapped to one of Conan's known remote exception types.

expectation.grounded: When REST client code handling remote responses encounters a non-success HTTP status code that is not present in the known EXCEPTION_CODE_MAPPING fallback set, it must raise ConanException with a message formatted as `Server exception <status_code>: <response_text>`. This fallback must be used consistently in the affected remote REST paths that previously attempted to instantiate a mapped exception from the status code.
expectation.conceptual: Users should receive a normal Conan error that explains the unexpected server response, including the numeric status code and message body, instead of seeing a secondary failure caused by Conan not recognizing that status code.

constraints.grounded: Known mapped HTTP error codes must continue to raise their existing Conan exception types with the original server text. The fallback behavior should apply only when no mapped exception exists for the returned status code, and it should preserve the underlying server response text in the surfaced error.
constraints.conceptual: This change should improve resilience and diagnostics for unusual or nonstandard server responses without changing the behavior of normal success cases or already supported error codes.

behavior: Remote REST methods now raise a ConanException fallback for unrecognized HTTP error codes instead of relying on a missing exception mapping.
The fallback error message includes both the returned HTTP status code and the server response text.
Known remote error codes continue to use their existing mapped Conan exception classes.
acceptance_criteria: When a Conan remote returns an unmapped HTTP error status such as `444`, the client operation should fail with ConanException rather than crashing due to a missing exception type.
When that fallback error is reported to the user, it should include the numeric status code and the response text from the server.
When a remote returns a recognized mapped error code, Conan should continue to raise the corresponding existing exception behavior instead of converting it to the generic fallback.
